title: Planes clip wings on Reagan National taxiway while queuing for takeoff; no injuries reported
summary: No injuries were reported but passengers, including several members of Congress, were shaken up when one plane clipped the wing of another on a taxiway at Washington Reagan National Airport on Thursday afternoon.
content:
By Thomas Robertson

No injuries were reported but passengers, including several members of Congress, were shaken up when one plane clipped the wing of another passenger jet on a taxiway at Washington Reagan National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on Thursday afternoon.

The Federal Aviation Administration said the wingtip of an American Airlines flight bound for Charleston, South Carolina, struck another American Airlines flight bound for JFK International Airport in New York around 12:45 p.m. on a taxiway at the crowded airport.

Roughly 80 people were on the plane to Charleston, and 71 for the flight to New York, according to American Airlines. The company said in a statement to The Associated Press that damage was limited to a winglet on each aircraft. It said both planes would be taken out of service for inspection and that replacement aircraft would take passengers to their destinations.

The Federal Aviation Administration said it’s investigating the collision.

Rep. Josh Gottheimer, a Democrat representing New Jersey’s 5th District, said in a post on X he was on the plane bound for New York and used the incident as a chance to remind people about the consequences of cuts to the FAA, saying they “weaken our skies and public safety.”

The flight bound for Charleston was moving on the taxiway and hit the plane bound for New York, which was stationary at the time of the incident, according to a social media post from Rep. Nick LaLota, a Republican representing New York’s 1st District, who was also on board.

Rep. Grace Meng, a Democrat representing New York’s 6th District, said everyone on board was OK and crews began repairing the plane’s wing after passengers returned to the gate.

The collision is the second between two aircraft at or near Reagan National Airport this year. On the night of Jan. 29, a military helicopter and American Airlines flight collided over the Potomac River near the airport, killing all 67 people on board both aircraft.

About two months after that, reports surfaced that commercial flights were allowed in the area when a military flyover team was moving through, and the military jets came within seconds of crossing into the path of an incoming passengflight.

– The Associated Press contributed to this report.
author: WTOP News
